lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: food safety, storage, and reheating

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic food safety, storage, and reheating task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a trusted adult present, the learner selects three real items from the household refrigerator or pantry, checks each against the provided safe-storage guidelines (such as refrigerator temperature range and typical shelf-life windows), and records whether each item is still safe.
safetyNotes: The learner only handles the stove, microwave, or oven for reheating with the trusted adult present the entire time.
If an item shows signs of spoilage such as an off smell, mold, or an expired shelf-life window, the learner does not taste it; the adult decides whether to discard it.
Completing this task sheet never certifies the safety check or reheating by itself; a guardian confirmation is required before the task counts as complete.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real refrigerator or pantry check and reheating session is not possible, the learner instead works from a provided list of ten food items with their storage location and age, sorts each into 'safe to keep' or 'needs attention' using the same safe-storage guidelines, and separately identifies the correct reheating method and target temperature or doneness sign for two of the listed items, explaining the reasoning for each choice.

materials: adult-or-local: access to the real household refrigerator or pantry with a trusted adult
learner-local: the provided safe-temperature and shelf-life guidance sheet
adult-or-local: a real food item to reheat and a safe way to reheat it (stove, microwave, or oven)
learner-local: paper or a notes app to record findings

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which item's condition most surprised you compared to your prediction, and explain one specific habit you will change about how you store or check food because of what you found.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Storage safety check accuracy: All three items are checked against the guidance sheet, and each safe/needs-attention call correctly matches the stated shelf-life or temperature information. | Reheating method and confirmation: The correct method and target temperature or doneness sign from the guidance sheet is named and confirmed by the adult. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner check three additional pantry items against the guidance sheet's shelf-life information and create a short written schedule noting which one they should recheck first and why, based on how close it is to its safe window's end.

duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: food safety, storage, and reheating worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult present, the learner selects three real items from the household refrigerator or pantry, checks each against the provided safe-storage guidelines (such as refrigerator temperature range and typical shelf-life windows), and records whether each item is still safe.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact food safety, storage, and reheating decision or action.
Model move 2: Before checking, predict which of three items you plan to check might already be past its safe window.
Model move 3: With your adult, check each of the three items against the guidance sheet's temperature and shelf-life information, and record the result for each.

Model check: Storage safety check accuracy: All three items are checked against the guidance sheet, and each safe/needs-attention call correctly matches the stated shelf-life or temperature information. | Reheating method and confirmation: The correct method and target temperature or doneness sign from the guidance sheet is named and confirmed by the adult.

resources.title: food safety, storage, and reheating action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for food safety, storage, and reheating.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: food safety, storage, and reheating coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult present, the learner selects three real items from the household refrigerator or pantry, checks each against the provided safe-storage guidelines (such as refrigerator temperature range and typical shelf-life windows), and records whether each item is still safe.
Coach direction: Before checking, predict which of three items you plan to check might already be past its safe window.
Learner prompt: Name the three items you plan to check and write your prediction for whether each is still safe, based only on what you remember about when it was stored.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: food safety, storage, and reheating complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, check each of the three items against the guidance sheet's temperature and shelf-life information, and record the result for each.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I checked item one against the guidance sheet and recorded whether it is safe to keep or needs attention.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I checked item two against the guidance sheet and recorded whether it is safe to keep or needs attention.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I checked item three against the guidance sheet and recorded whether it is safe to keep or needs attention.

Equal-access rule: If a real refrigerator or pantry check and reheating session is not possible, the learner instead works from a provided list of ten food items with their storage location and age, sorts each into 'safe to keep' or 'needs attention' using the same safe-storage guidelines, and separately identifies the correct reheating method and target temperature or doneness sign for two of the listed items, explaining the reasoning for each choice.

resources.title: food safety, storage, and reheating minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which item's condition most surprised you compared to your prediction, and explain one specific habit you will change about how you store or check food because of what you found.

Success checks: Storage safety check accuracy: All three items are checked against the guidance sheet, and each safe/needs-attention call correctly matches the stated shelf-life or temperature information. | Reheating method and confirmation: The correct method and target temperature or doneness sign from the guidance sheet is named and confirmed by the adult.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: food safety, storage, and reheating supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional food safety, storage, and reheating condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Storage safety check accuracy: All three items are checked against the guidance sheet, and each safe/needs-attention call correctly matches the stated shelf-life or temperature information. | Reheating method and confirmation: The correct method and target temperature or doneness sign from the guidance sheet is named and confirmed by the adult..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
